get.description:
The records library's catalog: every record, team records first, with
its category, rule, `value_kind` (which of an entry's figures it fills),
search `keywords` and `featured_rank`, and no holder (GET
/events/records/holders). `since_season` and `through_season` are the
stored data's window. Cacheable: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

Each named record's holder: the first entry of its list,
`tied_count`, how many share that value, and `top`, the list's first
three entries exactly as GET /events/records/{record_id} returns them;
null when no stored data qualifies. Cacheable: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

422: `ids` missing or empty, naming more than 24 records, repeating one,
or naming an unknown record.

parameters.description: 1 to 24 distinct record ids, comma-separated. Sort them, so the same set is the same cache entry.
parameters.name: ids

schema.description: 1 to 24 distinct record ids, comma-separated. Sort them, so the same set is the same cache entry.

get.description:
One page of a record's ranked list, which holds at most its top 100
entries (a tie at the 100th place is cut by the list's order); `total`
is how many it holds. Ordered by value (ascending for
team-worst-season, descending for every other), then date or season,
then id. Cacheable: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

404: an unknown record id. 422: `limit` outside 1-100 or `offset`
outside 0-99.

Every season with at least one stored game, of any type, newest
first, as "YYYY-YY".

schema.title: Response List Seasons Events Seasons Get

get.description:
The team that won four of the season's playoff games labelled "NBA
Finals", the runner-up and the series result. Until then all three are
null, in a 200.

422: a malformed season (not "YYYY-YY"). 404: a well-formed season with
no stored game.

The season's regular-season leader boards in one read, each its top
`limit`: points, assists, rebounds, blocks, steals, field goals made,
threes (per-game averages, then player id), field-goal and three-point
percentage (total made / attempted, then player id) and field goals and
threes attempted (per-game averages).

`complete` is true once the season has a champion. Every board needs
the games rule `GET .../leaders` applies to the regular season: from
2023-24, 65 games when complete and ceil(65 x T / 82), at most 65,
while in progress (T the most games any team has played); before that,
70 % of T, rounded up. The percentage boards also need 300 field goals
or 82 threes made, ceil(base x T / 82), at most the base, while in
progress. Each rule is named in the response.

422: a malformed season or `limit` outside 1-10. 404: a well-formed
season with no stored game.

The top players by per-game average of `stat` (`threes`: three-
pointers made) over their played games of `game_type`, then by player
id. Regular season: from 2023-24, 65 games once the season has a
champion and, while it is in progress, the games on pace for 65:
ceil(65 x T / 82), at most 65, T the most games any team has played;
before 2023-24, 70 % of T, rounded up. The playoffs have no minimum.
The response names the rule and the minimum.

422: a malformed season, an unknown `stat` or `game_type`, or `limit`
outside 1-50. 404: a well-formed season with no stored game.

Regular-season standings by conference, then division. Within a
conference: win percentage, then wins, then team name (`tie_break`;
the NBA's own tie-breakers are not applied). Only `regular` games count.

422: a malformed season (not "YYYY-YY"). 404: a well-formed season with
no stored game.

No pagination — the NBA team set is ~30 rows, small and stable
(YAGNI, wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x02-events.md).

get.description:
One team's season: its regular-season record with home and away
splits, and every one of its games that season, of every type, newest
first.

422: a malformed season (not "YYYY-YY"). 404: an unknown team, or a
well-formed season with no stored game.

BoardLeaderOut.description:
`teams` are the abbreviations the player played for in the counted
games. On a count board `value` is the per-game average, one place, and
`made`/`attempted` are null; on a percentage board `value` is made /
attempted as a 0-1 fraction, three places, with those totals.
BoardLeaderOut.title: BoardLeaderOut

BoxScorePlayerOut.description: One player who played: has minutes, possibly zero seconds.
BoxScorePlayerOut.title: BoxScorePlayerOut

ChampionOut.description:
GET /events/seasons/{season}/champion. `result` is the Finals score,
the champion's wins first ("4-2"). All three are null until a team has
won four Finals games.
ChampionOut.title: ChampionOut

DivisionStandingsOut.description: A division's teams, in their conference's order.
DivisionStandingsOut.title: DivisionStandingsOut

GameDetailOut.description:
GET /events/games/{id}: a read model built by
app.events.service.game_detail, not the ORM row.
GameDetailOut.title: GameDetailOut

LeaderBoardOut.description:
One board. `rule` names its qualifying rule; `minimum_made` is a
percentage board's made minimum (null on a count board).
LeaderBoardOut.title: LeaderBoardOut

LeaderBoardsOut.description:
GET /events/seasons/{season}/leader-boards. `complete`: the season
has a champion. `rule` names the games rule and `minimum_games` its
minimum, which every board applies.
LeaderBoardsOut.title: LeaderBoardsOut

LeaderOut.description:
`teams` are the abbreviations the player played for in the counted
games; `average` is per game, one place.
LeaderOut.title: LeaderOut

LeadersOut.description:
GET /events/seasons/{season}/leaders. `rule` names the qualifying
rule applied and `minimum_games` its minimum (0 for the playoffs).
LeadersOut.title: LeadersOut

PlayerDetailOut.description:
GET /events/players/{id}: a read model built by
app.events.service.player_detail. Only played rows of `regular` and
`playoffs` games count towards a line.
PlayerDetailOut.title: PlayerDetailOut

PlayerGameOut.description:
One row of GET /events/players/{id}/games: the player's box-score
line in one game, played or not, with the game around it. A row
without minutes (`seconds_played` null) is a did-not-play.
PlayerGameOut.title: PlayerGameOut

RecentGameOut.description: A completed matchup, with league ranks and regular records in its season.
RecentGameOut.title: RecentGameOut

RecordCatalogItemOut.description:
One record of the catalog (EVENTS-012): what it is, never who holds
it. `category` is one of the library's seven; `keywords` are the words
a search matches beside the title; `featured_rank` is 1 to 16 for the
featured records, in order, and null for every other.
RecordCatalogItemOut.title: RecordCatalogItemOut

RecordEntryOut.description:
One entry of a ranked record list. `rank` is competition ranking
(equal values share a rank, the next rank skips). `team` is the team
(for a player's single-game record, the team they played for), null for
a player's count or career sum; `season` and `game` are null where the
record has none. `value` is an integer, except a season record's win
percentage (a fraction from 0 to 1, three places).

The figures behind `value` (EVENTS-011), each null where the record's
`value_kind` does not use it: a win_loss record's `wins`, `losses` and
`pct` (the win percentage, equal to `value`); a made_total record's
`made` (equal to `value`), `attempted` and `pct` (null when nothing was
attempted); a shot_pct record's `made`, `attempted` and `pct` (equal to
`value`). An average's `value` is the mean, one place, with no figure
beside it. `pct` is a fraction from 0 to 1, three places.
RecordEntryOut.title: RecordEntryOut

RecordGameOut.description: The game a single-game record was set in, and the opponent.
RecordGameOut.title: RecordGameOut

RecordHolderOut.description:
The list's first entry; `tied_count` is how many entries share its
value (1 when it is alone). `top` (EVENTS-016) is the list's first three
entries (fewer when it holds fewer), each exactly as GET
/events/records/{record_id} returns it, in the list's order; the first
is this entry.
RecordHolderOut.title: RecordHolderOut

RecordHoldersOut.description:
GET /events/records/holders: one key per asked id, its holder or null
when no stored data qualifies.
RecordHoldersOut.title: RecordHoldersOut

RecordListOut.description:
GET /events/records/{record_id}: one page of the record's top 100
entries. `total` is how many entries the list holds (at most 100).
RecordListOut.title: RecordListOut

RecordOut.description:
A team's regular-season record (only `regular` games count: NBA Cup
group and knockout games do; play-in, playoffs and the cup final do
not), with home and away splits.
RecordOut.title: RecordOut

RecordsCatalogOut.description:
GET /events/records: every record, no holder. The data window is the
earliest and latest stored seasons, null when there are none.
RecordsCatalogOut.title: RecordsCatalogOut

SeasonLineOut.description:
One season and game type the player played in. `teams` are
abbreviations in the order first played; the stats are summed across
them, as nba.com's "TOT" row is.
SeasonLineOut.title: SeasonLineOut

ShootingOut.description:
Counting stats and shooting percentages, shared by a player's line
and a team's totals. Percentages are a fraction from 0 to 1, three
places, computed from made and attempted; null when none was attempted.
ShootingOut.title: ShootingOut

StandingRowOut.description:
`win_pct` is wins / games, three places. `games_behind` is in half
games behind the first team of the conference's order:
((leader_w - w) + (l - leader_l)) / 2.
StandingRowOut.title: StandingRowOut

StandingsOut.description:
GET /events/seasons/{season}/standings. `tie_break` names the
ordering rule: the NBA's own tie-breakers are not applied.
StandingsOut.title: StandingsOut

StatLineOut.description:
A career or season line: totals of the played rows, percentages
computed from the totals (the box score's rule) and per-game averages
to one place, null when no game was played.
StatLineOut.title: StatLineOut

TeamBoxScoreOut.description:
One team's side: played rows (starters first, then by seconds
played), the players who did not play, and totals summed from the
played rows, never adjusted to the final score.
TeamBoxScoreOut.title: TeamBoxScoreOut

TeamRefOut.description: A team as a game detail embeds it.
TeamRefOut.title: TeamRefOut

TeamSeasonGameOut.description: One of the team's games, from its side: `team_score` is its own.
TeamSeasonGameOut.title: TeamSeasonGameOut

TeamSeasonOut.description:
GET /events/teams/{team_id}/seasons/{season}: the regular-season
record and every game of every type, newest first.
TeamSeasonOut.title: TeamSeasonOut
